analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | tough sledding | transports | early EPS 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: Desk calls the backdrop challenging. S&P futures down 20bps pre-market, led lower by technology shares off over 100bps, with global markets still for sale amid credit and capital concerns after AI/data center updates from TSMC and others.
KOSPI closed down 757bps, triggering circuit breakers and entering a bear market. Japan down 490bps. France up 30bps, Germany down a similar amount.

Crude down 2% with Brent $104 and WTI $95. European gas down similarly to $85, near broadly new highs heading into cooler weather. 10-year yield down to 5.09% on growth concerns, DXY just below 102, Bitcoin $81.2k.

Early earnings season shows a very challenging backdrop despite muted stock moves. RPM missed Q1, guided Q2 below, and narrowed full-year guidance toward the low end on consumer end-market weakness, higher input inflation and healthcare/education weakness.
DAL missed Q3 and guided Q4/full year down on higher fuel. RASM is set to accelerate in Q4, but US airlines are starting to see demand elasticity, with TSA throughput turning down year over year.

FAST showed a larger than expected step back in September sales. The headline Q3 beat was more mixed underneath, with tariff and timing benefits to margins. Positioning in FAST was incrementally short heading in, likely the reason for the intraday rally.
JBHT reports tonight after already flagging sharply lower Q3 EPS. Focus is on demand and cost commentary and whether Q4/2027 estimates reset. Positioning skews negative but less extreme than FAST.
VAT Group (Europe) reported strong Q3 orders with book-to-bill of 1.9x, the highest ever. Estimates are likely to move up low double digits for Q4 and 2027.
RKLB down 9% pre-market after an update on Neutron development that pushes target launch timing into 2027. AIR announced a capital return plan with a dividend and $100mm buyback.

Jordan Alliger (GIR) transports Q3 preview: stay the course with Buy-rated trucking names, Truckload (KNX, WERN, SNDR) and LTL (ODFL, SAIA, ARCB, XPO, TFII). Trucking has pulled back (TL down 14%, LTL down 20%, broader transports down 10% since June 1), which GS sees as a chance to capture the usual rally into peak shipping season.

Supporting data for transports: channel checks show stable demand, US intermodal and industrial rail traffic up +5% and +2% at the start of 3Q after +5% and +3% in 2Q26, ISM near 55, positive spread between ISM new orders and inventories, and two consecutive positive CASS freight readings.

Truck supply remains tight due to regulation, so GS expects spot/contract price support even in a modest peak freight environment, barring negative volume. Used truck pricing is positive and Class 8 net orders are limited.

Transports 3Q26 estimates rise 1.5% on average. Brokers/LTL revisions are +7%/+3%, Rails -2%, TL -1%. GS lowered estimates for 6 companies, raised 7 and left 3 unchanged. Fuel surcharge lags versus the sharp diesel spike hurt rails and truckload, while LTL benefits.

A&D (Noah, AUSA takeaways): industry participants expect a small amount of reconciliation and/or supplemental spending on top of the $1.15tn FY27 base budget, with slower growth beyond FY27 given the high base.
Defense spending priorities are unmanned, counter-UAS, space, electronic warfare, hypersonics and munitions restocking. Companies are diversifying supply chains to ramp production.
GS recommends more defense tech than legacy defense on greater growth and margin expansion. Buy: HII (on CL), LHX, AVAV, AVEX, CACI, HAWK, KTOS, DRS, TDY. Sell: LMT, GD, MRCY, BAH.
Initial investor questions for earnings (bogeys): PCAR TP&O gross margins, NVT orders, MMM organic growth, and EMR, ROK, JCI, WWD guides.

tension_points.bull_case: Group pulled back (TL -14%, LTL -20%), truck supply is tight due to regulation, channel checks show stable demand, rail volumes are up and ISM is near 55, so peak season could bring a seasonal rally with spot and contract price support.
tension_points.bear_case: High energy prices and consumer resilience risk into peak shopping season, and fuel surcharge lags hurt rails and truckload in 3Q.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A negative volume situation in peak freight, which GS says would undermine the pricing support.
